chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ibn Fazzal, from various men, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who exclaims the Talbiyya seventy times while in his Ihram, with faith and considering it as a good deed, Allah will cause a thousand thousand angels to testify for him with freedom from the Fire, and freedom from hypocrisy.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.احْتِسَاباً: With expectation of reward/considering it a good deed
key_terms.لَبَّى: To exclaim the Talbiyya ('Here I am, O Allah') during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for reciting the Talbiyya seventy times during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration, transmitted through the prominent chain of al-Kulayni, highlights the spiritual efficacy of the Talbiyya as a means of securing divine testimony from a vast host of angels. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *i'timad* (sincere reliance) and *ihtisab* (expectation of reward) in ritual acts, linking the verbal declaration of Hajj directly to the removal of *nifaq* (hypocrisy) and *nar* (Hellfire).
